sources: Acker et al. — SIPA (age cutoffs ~1.22 / 1.0 / 0.9) outperforms adult SI and age-adjusted hypotension for transfusion, OR, ICU risk in pediatric trauma
McCarthy et al. — YOS 6–30 in febrile children classically 3–36 mo; ≤10 lower risk, ≥16 higher serious-illness risk; not a standalone infant-fever rule-out
Mintegi/Gomez Step-by-Step — febrile infants ≤90 d; low risk if well-appearing, >21 d, no leukocyturia, PCT <0.5, CRP ≤20, ANC ≤10k; may avoid LP/antibiotics/admission on pathway
ACOG PB 184 — TOLAC in facility with emergency cesarean; uterine rupture ~0.5–0.9% after prior low-transverse scar; Grobman nomogram for predicted VBAC success counseling
ACOG PB 222 — HTN after 20 weeks (or postpartum) + proteinuria or end-organ criteria; severe features → admit, MgSO₄, BP control, delivery planning
Sibai / Tennessee–Mississippi HELLP criteria — hemolysis + elevated LFTs + low platelets; partial HELLP managed as obstetric emergency with MgSO₄, serial labs, delivery planning
Obstetric MgSO₄ teaching — therapeutic ~4.8–8.4 mg/dL; loss of DTRs then respiratory depression; stop infusion, support airway, calcium gluconate 1 g IV; q1h RR/SpO2/DTRs/UOP checks
Clinical toxicology teaching — Widmark dose/distribution estimate and EtOH ≈ osm gap × 4.6 are bedside approximations; measured EtOH and workup for other alcohols when gap unexplained
Rumack–Matthew — single acute ingestion, timed level ≥4 h; US treatment (150) line; NAC if on/above line; may withhold NAC if clearly below line with certain time

issues: whenToUse limited tool to 'IV loading doses' despite bioavailability (F) options for oral routes; whyUse 'steady concentration' overstated (loading dose targets a concentration, not steady state by itself)
changes: whenToUse: 'Estimating IV loading doses when Vd and target level are known' → 'Estimating loading doses when Vd and target concentration are known'
whyUse: 'achieving steady concentration quickly' → 'rapidly achieving a target plasma concentration'
sources: Standard PK — LD = Cp × Vd × weight / F; loading rapidly approaches a target/therapeutic concentration; steady state still depends on maintenance dosing
Standard ICU drip math — mL/hr = mcg/kg/min × kg × 60 / (mcg/mL); independent double-check and smart-pump library
Standard hematology — corrected retic = retic% × (Hct/45); RPI adjusts for maturation; low RPI hypoproliferative workup; high RPI hemolysis/bleed
Standard lab hematology — ALC = WBC × lymph fraction; absolute counts preferred over %; severe lymphopenia → HIV/meds/immune eval; persistent adult lymphocytosis → smear/flow
Adrogué–Madias / US expert panel — Na deficit = TBW × (goal − actual) is adjunctive; severe symptoms: 100 mL 3% saline boluses (Europe often 150 mL); slow correction if chronic
Standard acid-base — expected PCO₂ ≈ 0.7×HCO₃ + 20 (±5); compensation via hypoventilation; mismatch suggests mixed disorder
Katz (+1.6) / Hillier (+2.4) glucose correction — translocational hyponatremia; corrected Na guides free-water/fluid planning in DKA/HHS (ADA)
Traub–Johnson — height-based pediatric IBW used in pharmacy dosing contexts; always check drug-specific TBW vs IBW vs adjusted weight
Modified Finnegan NAS — serial CNS/metabolic/GI scoring; non-pharm first; common pharmacologic thresholds ≥8 ×3 or ≥12 ×2 (morphine/methadone protocols institutional)
Classic NAGMA teaching — negative UAG suggests appropriate NH₄⁺ (e.g., diarrhea); positive suggests impaired renal acidification (RTA); use with urine pH and clinical context
